subject: DataHarbor integration plan & private onramp questions
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Brown <alex.brown@dataharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Integration discovery + private onramp checklist

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we can align with your network/security team. Please correct anything I missed.

Call highlights:
- DataHarbor is targeting a dedicated/private onramp for model inference (strict data controls, predictable throughput).
- Primary concerns: outbound egress control, cert-based mutual TLS for service-to-service auth, and limiting network paths to a VPC endpoint or peering.
- Desired features: structured tool-calling for document ingestion, embeddings for semantic search, and a small reranker for relevance tuning.

Immediate integration checkpoints (action items):
1) SDK & auth model
   - Recommend server-side Redwood SDK (Python/Node) with client-auth via short-lived service tokens.
   - For DataHarbor production, we advise mTLS on the Private deployment; fallback to API key for sandbox.
2) Private connectivity
   - VPC endpoint (our side) + customer egress rules: allowlist Redwood TLS endpoints + support for reserved IP ranges.
   - IP allowlist CSV needed from you for pre-prod/prod.
3) DNS & egress
   - We support DNS override or proxying through your egress; need to confirm whether outbound DNS resolution is via your resolver or a transit VPC.
4) Certs & rotation
   - Certificate exchange: we can support PKCS#12 or PEM bundles; automatic rotation via ACME/HSM integration is an option.
5) Embeddings & reranker
   - Suggest a test corpus (10k docs) to validate embedding latency and rerank quality.

Attached: Redwood onramp checklist and a template IP allowlist (redwood-onramp-checklist.xlsx, DH-2026-0813-non-prod-iplist.csv). Also attaching a short mTLS diagram for reference (dataharbor-mtls-diagram.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm whether mTLS is required for all traffic and share the non-prod IPs by EOD Mon (12/14).
- Us: draft an estimated timeline for Private onramp + an initial security profile (we'll include cert rotation cadence and KMS options).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your network/security (30–45 min).

I can schedule a follow-up — available Mon/Tue next week afternoons PT.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0112
---
Attachment stubs: redwood-onramp-checklist.xlsx (13 KB), dataharbor-mtls-diagram.pdf (48 KB)

From: Alex Brown <alex.brown@dataharbor.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataHarbor IT <it@dataharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap: Integration discovery + private onramp checklist

Thanks, Tessa — appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- mTLS requirement: security policy requires mTLS for all outbound traffic to third-party inference providers in prod. Sandbox can use API key for testing but must be isolated.
- VPC approach: we'd prefer a customer-managed NAT + VPC peering to Redwood's private endpoint rather than proxying through a transit VPC. Can you confirm support for that topology?
- Cert rotation: we use an internal PKI with automatic rotation; can Redwood accept our signed certs and accept a certificate chain from our CA?
- KMS: Key management must integrate with our AWS KMS; will Redwood support KMS-backed key wrapping for any sensitive tokens/cert secrets?

Also: procurement/contract questions — we'll need standard SOC2+ clause and an indemnity addendum pushed by our legal team. I'll loop in procurement once we lock the technical topology.

Attaching our network diagram and sample IP allocation for your reference.

Alex
Director, Cloud Ops | DataHarbor
alex.brown@dataharbor.com
---
Attachment stubs: dataharbor-network-diagram.vsdx (290 KB), dh-ip-sample.csv (2 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: DataHarbor deal motion & constraints (DH-2026-0813)

Tessa / Lauren — quick internal note after Alex's reply. Key sales/ops points:

- mTLS required in prod -> treat this as Private deployment (not Hosted). We should price for Dedicated/Private SKU.
- Topology: customer-managed NAT + VPC peering is supported but will require networking intake (we need VPC CIDRs, peering constraints, and peering autoscaling notes).
- KMS integration: engineering flagged a JIRA to validate AWS KMS HSM support for wrapping tokens; will need SE to confirm time to enable.
- Timeline ask from customer: 8–10 weeks to production. Let's propose an 8-week phased plan: 2 weeks design & network intake, 3 weeks infra & cert exchange, 2 weeks integration + embed/rerank pilot, 1 week hardening & audit.

Action items (internal):
- Lauren: draft the technical intake template and schedule SE call with DataHarbor IT (target next Wed 12/16).
- Laura: prepare Dedicated pricing estimate + amendment language for SOC2/indemnity clauses to hand to procurement.
- Tessa: coordinate cert exchange details and confirm sandbox API-key flow for their devs.

Ben
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Integration discovery + private onramp checklist

Alex — thanks for the confirmations and for sharing the diagram. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

- Topology: We confirm support for customer-managed NAT + VPC peering to Redwood Private endpoints. We'll need the VPC CIDR ranges and a point of contact at your network team to open the peering request.
- mTLS & certs: We can accept your signed certs and support your CA chain. For rotation, we recommend a 90-day cadence; Redwood can optionally automate rotation if you allow our orchestration role in a scoped KMS/HSM integration.
- KMS: We support AWS KMS integration for key wrapping. Engineering will validate an HSM-backed flow in the SE call.
- SOC2/legal: Noted — we'll surface an amendment for SOC2 + indemnity redline to your procurement. Ben's team will own commercial terms.

Follow-ups / calendar:
- Technical deep-dive w/ SE and your network/security: Wed, 16 Dec 2026, 10:00–10:45 PT — invite sent (https://cal.com/redwood/tessa-dataharbor-30m).
- Please upload the non-prod IP list to the shared Drive link (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e6f/view).

I'll attach the network intake template in the follow-up and share our cert exchange checklist ahead of the SE call. If anything is urgent, loop Ben for procurement and Lauren for intake.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0112
